text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: egress error spike in eu-west-2 (zone a). Multiple services reporting 502/504 to external APIs and synthetic checks failing. Metric: egress-errors / 5m = 12x baseline. Pager: paging on-call. https://internal.monitoring/reports/3945678901
Alice SRE: I'm on it. Acknowledging incident, paging networking and infra. Starting timeline.
Bob Support: Getting customer reports — some customers seeing webhooks timeout and failed uploads. Support ticket count up ~18 in last 10m. Notified account owners for the top 3 affected.
Carol NetEng: looking at VPC route tables + NAT health. Quick check: one private subnet in eu-west-2a shows route to nat-02b (unhealthy) after recent rollout. Seems route-table association flipped.
Dave Infra: we rolled a tf apply 10m ago around nat autoscaling changes. Could be a race. I'm checking the apply logs.
Alice SRE: Can we fail traffic to nat-02a or re-associate subnet to correct RT? What's safer for fastest mitigation?
Carol NetEng: safest quick mitigation is to update the subnet's route table association to the standby route table that points to nat-02a (healthy). I'll prepare the CLI command.
Carol NetEng: ```bash
# re-associate subnet to the standby route table
aws ec2 replace-route-table-association --association-id rtbassoc-0abcd1234 --route-table-id rtb-standby-eu2a --region eu-west-2
```
Dave Infra: FYI association IDs vary per subnet, I'll run a small script to map and re-associate only affected subnets.
Bob Support: any ETA? Customers asking for ETA.
Alice SRE: Carol/Dave, once assoc is swapped, we'll run canary pings and watch conntrack and NAT metrics. Aim for 5-10m.
Carol NetEng: Doing a targeted re-assoc for subnet-priv-a-east now. Executing: `replace-route-table-association assoc-0f1e2d3c rtb-standby-eu2a` -> OK.
sre-oncall: Noted. Running curl checks to external endpoints from a pod in the subnet.
sre-oncall: curl https://httpbin.org/status/200 -> 200 OK. Good.
Alice SRE: Observability — egress error rate down by 60% in the affected AZ. Synthetic checks returning to normal.
Bob Support: Tickets updating — customers reporting restored uploads. Leaving a note in each ticket.
Carol NetEng: Root cause looks like a route table association drift after terraform split-module apply; the association resource appears non-deterministic in order when parallel applies touched nat modules. Terraform plan didn't show drift before apply.
Dave Infra: We'll add a lock step in the pipeline to ensure route-table-assoc changes happen after NAT provisioning, and add a post-apply validation: query associations and validate egress path.
Alice SRE: Temporary mitigation completed. Monitoring for 30m. I'll mark P0 -> P1 if stable.
Bob Support: Pushed status update to status.redwood.ai saying degraded -> resolved for eu-west-2a egress.
Carol NetEng: Noting additional oddness: DNS cache on app side held references to the old NAT egress IP (private SNAT). TTLs are long (cached by proxy). We're forcing a small DNS bounce on impacted frontends.
Alice SRE: Action items captured: 1) Pipeline change to sequence TF applies, 2) Post-apply validation job, 3) Add alert for unexpected route-table-assoc changes, 4) Postmortem to infra/net in 24h.
Dave Infra: I'll own the pipeline change.
Carol NetEng: I'll own the validation job and the alert.
Bob Support: I'll coordinate customer comms and compile impacted account list.
Alice SRE: Handoff: I'm on for 20 more minutes, then handing to next on-call. If anything regresses, re-pager. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident updated: severity -> mitigated. Duration so far 12m. Incident channel pinned runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/internet-egress-issue
Alice SRE: Logging final note before handoff: keep the incident open until 30m stable window. We'll kick off the postmortem template after stabilization.
